drivingQuestion: How could Pishon's married wife refuse, according to Beit Shammai?

segments.he: מִדְּקָא אָכֵיל פֵּירֵי, פְּשִׁיטָא נְשׂוּאָה הִיא. וְהָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי נְשׂוּאָה לָא מְמָאֲנָה! תְּרֵי קִיטְרֵי עֲבַדוּ בֵּיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Since he was consuming the profits» from her property, «it is obvious that» it is speaking of a case where «she was married,» as a man is not entitled to the profits of the property of his betrothed. «But didn’t Beit Shammai say that a married» minor girl «cannot perform refusal?» The Gemara answers in accordance with Beit Shammai’s opinion: «They tied him in two knots,» i.e., the Sages punished Pishon in two ways: They permitted the refusal against him to take place in his absence, and they permitted it even though she was already married to him.
